info.bio:
Formado en 1985 por Vince Clarke en los sintetizadores, antiguo co-fundador y ex-integrante de Depeche Mode y el cantante Andy Bell. 

Vince Clarke después del éxito obtenido al lado de Depeche Mode, abandonó el proyecto para pasar a formar una sociedad con la cantante Alison Moyet, Yazoo, y The Assembly con Feargal Sharkey y Paul Quinn.

Clarke puso un anuncio en el periódico musical Melody Maker de Londres donde decía que buscaba un vocalista para su nueva producción.

scenes.name: Synth-pop y new romantics
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Todo empieza con los instrumentos electrónicos, el futurismo melódico de Eno y los ritmos robóticos de Kraftwerk: el synth-pop es quizá el acontecimiento más importante de la música melódica desde el Mersey-beat. The Buggles («Video Killed The Radio Star»), Gary Numan, Yellow Magic Orchestra, OMD, Depeche Mode, Human League; con Soft Cell llega el diluvio y el dúo de teclista y cantante se impone (Eurythmics, Yazoo, Erasure, Pet Shop Boys). Flying Lizards y New Order («Blue Monday»). Los nuevos ídolos adolescentes, los new romantics: Duran Duran, Culture Club, Thompson Twins, Tears For Fears, ABC, Heaven 17.

podcast.title: "Four Minutes and 33 Seconds" Cover
podcast.body: Erasure was included in a 2019 box set from Mute Records, which featured numerous artists performing covers of John Cage's silent work, "Four Minutes and 33 Seconds." "mute records compiled a bunch of them in a box set featuring... erasure..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

podcast.title: 12-inch Remix Business
podcast.body: Erasure joined other bands in the 1980s in releasing 12-inch remixes, a format that gained prominence after New Order's "Blue Monday." This was instrumental in their appeal to dance club audiences. "And so was Depeche Mode and The Cure and The Human League and Simple Minds and The Cult and Killing Joke and Erasure and Psychedelic Furs and Madness. They all got into the 12-inch business."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Andy Bell's Role in Songwriting and Interpretation
podcast.body: Although Vince Clarke is recognized as the primary creative force behind Erasure's music, nearly all songs are credited as band collaborations. Andy Bell's unique romantic, dreamy, and expressive vocal interpretations significantly reinvented Clarke's songwriting style, completing the group's sound. "toda la música y todas las canciones de Eres y Or están prácticamente todas firmadas a medias, como banda, aunque realmente el elemento creativo es Vince Clark."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Continued Parallel Projects by Members
podcast.body: Even after achieving success, Erasure members Vince Clarke and Andy Bell continued to pursue their own creative endeavors. Vince Clarke maintained his various projects due to his immensely creative nature, and Andy Bell also had a complementary solo project, demonstrating their ongoing artistic output outside the main band. "Vince Clark ha seguido teniendo sus proyectos porque es una versión enormemente creativa y otra cosa importantísima es el trabajo que hizo Andy Bell dentro de las comunidades homosexuales."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Formation from a Single-Song Collaboration
podcast.body: Erasure's formation began when Andy Bell was initially approached to sing one or two songs for another of Vince Clarke's projects. However, their immediate connection and compatibility led them to quickly form a stable new band instead, heading straight to the recording studio shortly after meeting. "Antivel inicialmente iba a cantar una o dos canciones de otro de los proyectos de Vince Clark que al final se juntan para formar una nueva banda de forma estable."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Initial Commercial Failure and Critical Reception
podcast.body: Erasure's early singles and debut album, *Wonderland*, did not achieve the commercial success typically associated with Vince Clarke's projects. Critics were harsh, and the band found themselves playing in small venues, a stark contrast to Clarke's previous stadium-filling acts. "el lanzamiento del álbum que fue rápido finalmente no terminó siendo un éxito, es curioso porque Vince Clark venía de un momento en el que prácticamente todo lo que hacía era un éxito rotundo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Pioneering 80s Keyboard-Bass Alt Rock
podcast.body: Erasure was listed as a "keyboard bass band" from the 1980s, whose music was a staple for alternative kids dancing before the rise of grunge, and whose electronic dance attitude experienced a revival in the 2000s. "25 years earlier, long before Grunge guitars took over, alternative kids danced to keyboard bass bands like Depeche Mode, New Order, OMD, Durand Iran, the Human League, Eurasia, Eurythmics, and so many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Professionalism During Early Struggles
podcast.body: Despite the initial lack of success for *Wonderland* and the critical reception, Vince Clarke and Andy Bell maintained an incredibly professional attitude. They continued performing in small venues and endured the album's limited traction, showcasing their dedication as musicians. "siguieron dando sus conciertos en pequeñas salas, siguieron aguentando el escaso tirón del disco."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Prominent Technopop Band
podcast.body: Erasure was highlighted as a Technopop band that enjoyed significant popularity, contributing to the genre's presence on both alternative music stations and mainstream pop charts. "Petchop boys, Urythmix, Erasure, More Depeche Mode."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Two-Person Synthpop Model
podcast.body: Listed as an example of a synthpop band that adopted the common two-person model, featuring a singer or front person alongside a composer, programmer, and operator. "Yes, E-Rature, the pet shop boys, Eurythmics. Many of them had this two-person model."

xref.title: Covers Compilation Box Set (2019)
xref.body: In 2019, Mute Records released a box set featuring various artists covering John Cage's "Four Minutes and 33 Seconds." The compilation included more than 50 artists, such as Depeche Mode, New Order, Moby, Erasure, and Afghan Whigs, all performing a piece consisting of silence. "More than 50 artists playing nothing."

xref.title: Founding Mute Records
xref.body: Using the profits from "Warm Leatherette," Daniel Miller established his own independent record label, Mute, dedicated exclusively to guitar-less music, which later introduced artists like Depeche Mode, Erasure, and Yazoo. "He took the profits and founded his own independent record label devoted entirely to guitar less music. He called the label Mute."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
